notes: 2026 tax computation schedules (Form K-40ES 2026): 5.2% up to $23,000 (single/HoH/MFS) or $46,000 (MFJ), 5.58% above.

Standard deduction $3,605 single, $8,240 MFJ, $6,180 HoH (K.S.A. 79-32,119; same on the 2026 K-40ES chart). Exemption $9,160 single/HoH and $18,320 MFJ, plus an extra $2,320 for head of household (K.S.A. 79-32,121 / 79-32,121b, fixed amounts for 2025 and later, not indexed; TY2025 K-40 instructions apply the HoH extra $2,320).

Not modeled: $2,320 dependent exemptions, higher standard deduction for age 65+/blind, itemized deductions, Kansas modifications on Schedule S (e.g., Social Security/retirement subtractions), food sales and other credits.

seDeduction.note: Inherited: Kansas AGI starts from federal AGI.

retirementContributions.note: SEP-IRA and solo 401(k) deductions are inherited through federal AGI.

qbi.note: The federal QBI deduction is below AGI; Kansas applies its own standard deduction and exemptions instead.

localIncomeTax.note: Kansas cities and counties do not levy a local earned-income tax on individuals.

estimatedTax.threshold: Required if your estimated Kansas tax after withholding and credits is $500 or more and withholding/credits may be less than the smaller of 90% of 2026 tax or 100% of 2025 tax.
estimatedTax.safeHarbor: No penalty if each payment is timely and total payments/credits are at least 90% of 2026 tax, or at least 100% of the 2025 tax (12-month return with a liability), or 90% of annualized-income tax (Schedule K-210). The Jan 15 installment is not required if the 2026 return is filed and paid in full by Jan 31, 2027.

businessCosts.llcFormationFee: $85 online or $90 on paper for Articles of Organization (Form DL instructions rev. 2/27/26).
businessCosts.annualReportFee: Information Report every two years (biennial, due April 15 of the odd or even year matching formation year): $90 online or $110 on paper.
